title: Senate installs new chiefs for U.S. military space acquisition, spy satellites
summary: The U.S. Senate has appointed new leaders for military space acquisition and spy satellites. Erich Hernandez-Baquero will oversee military space acquisition, while Roger Mason will lead the National Reconnaissance Office.

title: FCC Space Bureau deputy takes the reins amid licensing overhaul
summary: The FCC has appointed Jennifer Gilsenan, deputy chief of its Space Bureau, to lead its satellite regulatory overhaul as Jay Schwarz prepares to retire. The move aims to maintain momentum in licensing reforms amid leadership transition.

title: U.S. Senate confirms Schiess to lead Space Force
summary: The U.S. Senate has confirmed Schiess as the new leader of the Space Force, marking a key transition as the military branch prepares for expansion and reforms. The appointment comes amid plans for rapid growth and acquisition changes within the Space Force.

title: Europe increases size and cost of IRIS² constellation
summary: The European Commission has agreed with an industrial consortium to expand the IRIS² secure connectivity constellation, increasing both the number of satellites and the overall cost.

title: Bipartisan Senate bill would sharpen Space Force training for conflict with China
summary: A bipartisan Senate bill proposes expanding space wargaming and an unclassified assessment of China's commercial space sector to enhance Space Force training for potential conflicts. The bill, introduced by Sens. Cortez Masto and Britt, aims to sharpen the Space Force's readiness amid rising tensions with China.

title: How should Europe’s militaries respond to space threats
summary: A panel of experts discusses Europe's defense strategy and response to space threats in a SpaceNews session. The discussion focuses on Europe's military posture in space.

title: Lessons for the future of NASA Mars exploration from a 1970s mission
summary: NASA's Viking 1 Mars landing on July 20, 1976, marked a historic robotic spaceflight achievement. The mission offers valuable lessons for future NASA Mars exploration efforts.

title: Redwire to fly dedicated Starfall mission for microgravity research
summary: Redwire's subsidiary will conduct microgravity research using SpaceX's Starfall reentry vehicle. The mission is dedicated to advancing space biotech and pharmaceutical applications.

title: Three companies building the tech to grow crops on the moon
summary: Three companies are developing technology to grow crops on the moon as part of the commercial space industry's focus on lunar exploration. This initiative aims to support future human missions and sustainable lunar habitats.

title: Rocket Lab launches 8th iQPS satellite
summary: Rocket Lab successfully launched its 8th iQPS radar-imaging satellite for Japan on August 6, following a previous launch attempt that was aborted over a month earlier.

title: SpaceX serious about building factories on the moon: 'It’s going to happen,' Elon Musk says
summary: SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, has expressed strong intentions to construct factories on the Moon, leveraging robotic systems for heavy lifting. This announcement was made during SpaceX's inaugural quarterly earnings call.

title: 'Not looking good right now': Starship likely to be lost at sea 2 weeks after epic 13th test flight, Elon Musk says
summary: SpaceX's Starship upper stage is unlikely to be recovered after its 13th test flight, as it remains adrift at sea two weeks later. Elon Musk acknowledged the grim outlook despite ongoing towing efforts.

title: NASA figured out how to keep its 48-year-old Voyager 2 probe running for yet another year
summary: NASA successfully extended the lifespan of its Voyager 2 probe by reducing its power usage, allowing it to continue operating its science instruments for another year. Launched in 1977, the probe is now in interstellar space.

title: Inside the mystery of the James Webb Space Telescope's little red dots — and how they might be evolving
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has observed strange 'little red dots' that may be evolving into spiral galaxies. These findings could reshape our understanding of early galaxy formation.

title: How to safely observe eclipses and the solar surface with a smart telescope
summary: A smart telescope like the Unistellar eQuinox 2 with a matching filter allows safe observation of solar events such as eclipses. The Aug. 12 total solar eclipse can be captured effortlessly using this method.

title: NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters will wear tiny capes
summary: NASA's Mars helicopters, part of the SkyFall mission, will be equipped with advanced technology integrated into tiny capes. This innovation aims to enhance their capabilities during future Mars exploration.

title: Engineers race to save stricken LINK rescue spacecraft before it's too late
summary: Engineers are working to rescue the stricken LINK rescue spacecraft, which was launched to save a NASA space telescope. Progress is being made in addressing the issue.

title: Chinese company Landspace targets Aug. 10 for historic rocket launch and landing attempt
summary: Chinese commercial launch company Landspace is preparing for its second attempt to catch and land an orbital rocket on August 10. This marks a historic milestone for China's private space sector.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 7, 1980: NASA's Viking 1 Mars orbiter shuts down 4 years into a 90-day mission
summary: NASA's Viking 1 Mars orbiter concluded its mission on Aug. 7, 1980, after operating for four years beyond its planned 90-day duration. The orbiter provided critical data about Mars during its extended mission.

title: Cosmic treasure chest explodes with baby stars | Space photo of the day for Aug. 7, 2026
summary: The Carina Nebula is featured as a 'space photo of the day' showcasing a cosmic region bursting with new star formation. This stunning image highlights the nebula's vibrant stellar nursery.

title: 2026 IGARSS Hyperwall Schedule
summary: NASA will showcase its Hyperwall storytelling at the IGARSS 2026 event, featuring sessions on Earth science technology and missions. The agenda includes talks by NASA experts like Mike Seablom and Karen St. Germain.

title: NASA’s IXPE Studies Magnetar
summary: Scientists using NASA’s IXPE conducted 140+ hours of observations of magnetar 1E 1547-5408, potentially capturing empty space behaving as predicted by physicists for 90 years.

title: NASA’s Lunar Development and Test Facility Prepares Artemis Hardware for Moon
summary: NASA's Lunar Development and Test Facility is preparing Artemis hardware to withstand the harsh lunar environment, including the challenge of abrasive and clinging Moon dust, ahead of astronauts' return to the Moon's surface.

title: APOD: 2026 August 7 – Rubin’s Cosmos Field
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 7, 2026, features Rubin's Cosmos Field, showcasing a significant astronomical observation. The image highlights the contributions of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory to deep-space research.

title: Sensing the Poles’ Hidden Heat
summary: NASA's PREFIRE mission has released new animations showing two years of seasonal temperature changes in the Arctic and Antarctic. These visualizations highlight previously unseen thermal variations at the poles.

title: Educators & Teens Get Hands-On With TEMPO Data to Help Investigate Local Air Quality
summary: NASA's CosmicDS project, led by Harvard University, partnered with the Smithsonian Institution's BEST AQI project to provide educators and teens with hands-on experience using TEMPO data for local air quality investigations in July 2026.

title: NASA’s SkyFall Helicopters at Work (Artist’s Concept)
summary: NASA has conceptualized three SkyFall Mars helicopters designed to collect subsurface radar data and near-infrared imagery from the Martian surface. The artist's concept illustrates their dual data collection capabilities using green and red beams.

title: Antenna Testing for NASA’s SkyFall Mission
summary: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory is conducting antenna testing for the SkyFall mission in an electromagnetic interference testing chamber. The test aims to minimize reflections and interferences to accurately measure the antenna pattern.

title: I Am Artemis: Tom Percy
summary: NASA is accelerating its Artemis missions for long-term lunar and Martian exploration, with Tom Percy leading systems engineering and integration for the Human Landing System Program. Percy collaborates with providers like SpaceX to advance these plans.

title: Taking Flight to Prepare for Space
summary: NASA astronaut Adam Fuhrmann trains for future space missions aboard NASA's WB-57 aircraft, simulating high-altitude conditions in pressure suits. The July 16, 2026, training prepares crews for ISS, Moon, or other missions.

title: Relativity Space engine integration milestone for Terran-R first stage
summary: Relativity Space achieved a key milestone in engine integration for the first stage of its reusable Terran-R rocket. This progress marks a significant advancement in the development of the company's next-generation launch vehicle.

title: Crew-13 pilot reflects on career, training, and upcoming science ahead of flight to ISS
summary: NASA has moved up the next International Space Station mission, Crew-13, with the pilot reflecting on their career and upcoming scientific goals. The mission aims to advance research and training ahead of the flight.

title: While SpaceX recovers Ship 40, Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14
summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean, while Ship 41 is being prepared for testing ahead of Flight 14.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first full week of August is expected to be busy with multiple space launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The launch manifest highlights a significant period for space industry activity.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing’s CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the International Space Station (ISS) by 2026. CEO Kelly Ortberg mentioned ongoing redesign efforts for the spacecraft.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has completed two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase while retrofitting efforts continue on Pad 1 for Block 3 flights.

title: Blue Origin continues rebuilding LC-36, prepares testing alternatives for New Glenn second stage
summary: Blue Origin is continuing the rebuilding of Launch Complex 36 (LC-36) and exploring alternative testing methods for the second stage of its New Glenn rocket following a recent pad explosion during a static fire test.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 successfully completed its mission with Ship 40 returning intact, demonstrating flawless performance. This achievement paves the way for future missions, including potential catch attempts.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket launch in China and a Falcon 9 mission. The launches highlight ongoing activity in global spaceflight operations.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft has revealed surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io after two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the moon's volcanic activity and geology.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) released a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over its 50-year history. The publication celebrates milestones across its missions and contributions to space exploration.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software on the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This presents a unique opportunity for testing and innovation in a deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A drone test flight at ESA's ESTEC facility in the Netherlands demonstrated a student-developed radar retroreflector technology. This marks the first flight of the payload, transitioning from drone use to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with two satellites to create an artificial solar eclipse for studying the Sun's corona. The coronagraph will block the Sun's disk, allowing the outer atmosphere to be observed.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with the European space industry on September 16-17. The event aims to facilitate idea exchange, capability showcasing, and partnership exploration.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: Next-generation antennas are being enhanced with advanced silicon-based technologies to improve performance and efficiency. This innovation is driving advancements in communication systems for space applications.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, ensuring its electronics are fit for space. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Redwire Books Starfall’s First Dedicated Mission
summary: Redwire subsidiary SpaceMD has secured a contract to transport up to 32 mini-labs on a future SpaceX Starfall mission. This marks the first dedicated mission for Redwire's Starfall initiative.

title: Op-ed: Aging Weather Satellites Are Raising Risks for America. It’s Time for a Hybrid Solution.
summary: Aging weather satellites are increasing risks for the U.S., prompting calls for a hybrid solution to improve military weather data quality and availability. The op-ed emphasizes the need for enhanced satellite capabilities to maintain strategic advantages.

title: Scaleup Europe Fund Makes its First Space Bet
summary: The Scaleup Europe Fund has made its first investment in the space sector, signaling a potential end to Europe's capital drought. This move highlights growing investor interest in European space startups.

title: Endeavor Optical Networks Emerges from Stealth
summary: Endeavor Optical Networks has come out of stealth mode to develop a constellation of optical communications satellites. The company aims to advance space-based optical communication technology.

title: Rocket Lab Wins $397M Contract to Build and Launch Threat-Tracking ‘Flatellites’
summary: Rocket Lab has secured a $397 million contract to develop and launch 'Flatellites' for threat-tracking purposes. This deal reinforces Rocket Lab's integrated approach to space operations, covering both satellite manufacturing and launch services.

title: SpaceX Reports Q2 Earnings
summary: SpaceX released its Q2 earnings after a record-breaking June IPO, with headline figures exceeding expectations.

title: Neuraspace Raises €15.6M to Scale its SDA Service
summary: Neuraspace has secured €15.6 million in funding to expand its Space Domain Awareness (SDA) services. The investment comes as the satellite population grows and defense ministries prioritize space as a critical domain.

title: FL Governor Candidate Launches Space Race Policy
summary: A Florida gubernatorial candidate has unveiled a space race policy to attract launches, investments, and high-paying jobs to the state. The initiative aims to compete with other states and countries for space industry opportunities.

title: Xona Clears Final Regulatory Hurdle for PNT Constellation
summary: Xona Space Systems has secured FCC approval to broadcast Pulsar navigation signals from its full satellite constellation, marking the final regulatory hurdle before scaling deployment.

title: Kreios Taps Kongsberg NanoAvionics for 2028 VLEO Demo
summary: Kreios has selected Kongsberg NanoAvionics to support its 2028 Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) demonstration mission, aiming to validate the company's ABEP thruster performance at various altitudes below Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

title: SES, Eutelsat Complete RDV1 Milestone for Europe’s IRIS2 Sovereign Constellation Program
summary: SES and Eutelsat have completed the RDV1 milestone for Europe's IRIS² sovereign constellation program. This achievement marks a significant step in the implementation phase of the program.

title: CEO Fallacher Suggests Eutelsat is ‘Undervalued’ Compared to SpaceX Following 2025-26 Results
summary: Eutelsat's CEO Fallacher stated the company is undervalued compared to SpaceX following strong growth in its LEO business segment for 2025-2026. The company reported significant progress in its fiscal year results.

title: How the Internet of Space is Reshaping Active Resiliency
summary: Satellite data is crucial for disaster assessment and emergency response, enabling better understanding of impacts like wildfires. The Internet of Space is enhancing active resiliency through advanced satellite technologies.

title: BlackSky Reports Record Service Revenue and International Growth From Gen-3 Adoption
summary: BlackSky reported record service revenue of $33 million in Q2 2026, driven by the adoption of its Gen-3 satellite solutions and international growth.

title: Gilat Demonstrates Interference Detection and Cancellation Technology
summary: Gilat Satellite Networks demonstrated interference detection and cancellation technology for satellite communications, marking a milestone for operations in contested spectrum environments.

title: BlackStar Orbital Takes SPAC Deal
summary: BlackStar Orbital Technologies, a company developing a reusable spacecraft platform, plans to go public through a SPAC merger with Pono Capital. This move aims to accelerate its growth and development in the space industry.

title: MatSing Details Manufacturing Technology to Improve Satellite Antenna Performance
summary: MatSing introduced a proprietary manufacturing technology to enhance satellite antenna performance, enabling multibeam and wideband capabilities for simultaneous signal transmission and reception across various directions and frequencies.

title: Capella, Iceye US, and Umbra Receive NRO Commercial SAR Contracts
summary: Capella Space, Iceye US, and Umbra have been awarded sole source contracts by the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) for commercial synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery under the Radar Commercial Augmentation (RCA) program.

title: SpaceX Outlines Starlink Mobile Plans in First Earnings Report
summary: SpaceX reported $7.8 billion in Q2 earnings, nearly doubling year-over-year, and outlined ambitious plans for Starlink Mobile. The company aims for $100 billion in annual recurring revenue.

title: Viasat Previews ViaSat-3 Satellites Entering Service in Q1 Results
summary: Viasat reported flat revenue of $1.2 billion for Q1 of its 2027 fiscal year. The company also previewed the entry into service of its ViaSat-3 satellites.
